Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop startup and initial policy/configuration resolution on Windows or macOS
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The main process constructs service wrappers without loading the native module. The native module and first OS watcher are created only when policy definitions or managed settings are initialized; policy configuration waits for the native policy result, while the managed-settings channel client starts its initial request in the background and account-policy initialization may later await it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer calls getManagedSettings or updatePolicyDefinitions on the main-process native managed-settings channel and receives change events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One background getManagedSettings call per renderer client/window; all cold calls converge on one main-process initialization. Definition updates are event-driven, not per policy item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC calls, coalescing, and cardinality used policy-watcher 1.4.0 before the dependency version changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The background client request is off initial workbench construction, but account-policy initialization can await the coalesced result. Definition updates await the corresponding IPC call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the native addon, read the Windows registry or macOS managed preferences, and establish an OS policy-change watcher.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One watcher per service/definition set, with at most the regular policy watcher and one centrally shared managed-settings watcher in the desktop main process; replacements occur only when definition sets change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Version 1.4.0 was loaded at these same sites with the same service count, serialization, and arguments. The diff supplies no evidence that 1.6.0 adds reads, polling, or watcher fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial regular policy resolution is on configuration initialization's critical path. Managed-settings initialization is background-started but can become part of account-policy readiness. Subsequent callbacks are event-driven.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Policy-definition count and renderer-window count. One native policy watcher is created for the product policy set; the main-process managed-settings service coalesces all window initialization requests onto one initialization promise and one watcher.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: NativePolicyService serializes watcher replacement through a Throttler. NativeManagedSettingsService coalesces non-forced initialization and serializes creation/replacement through a Throttler; separate renderer windows can issue IPC concurrently but do not create separate OS watchers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Within a process, the managed-settings initialization promise is the warm-cache/coalescing state; repeated initialization reuses it. Equal managed-setting definition sets return the existing initialization. A new process starts cold and creates its own bounded watcher set. Failures clear the managed-settings initialization promise for an explicit retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the unchanged repository-level load placement, watcher cardinality, coalescing, and critical paths; insufficient evidence of any regressive mechanism inside the upgraded artifact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The internal native implementation changed between package versions but its source, measurements, and behavior changes are not present in the supplied diff, so no increased CPU, I/O, memory, or latency can be established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff changes only the dependency version and lockfile artifact identity; it does not move native work earlier, increase watcher count, defeat coalescing, or alter concurrency in repository code.

Scenarios.Scenario: Policy-definition refresh and native policy change propagation during a desktop session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration/account events update policy definitions, then await an IPC call to the main process and any serialized watcher replacement. Native OS change callbacks update maps and fan out an IPC event to subscribed renderer clients.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a whole definition dictionary to the centralized main-process service and broadcast managed-setting changes back to renderer subscribers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per effective definition refresh and one event per native update per subscribed renderer; not per policy key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical calls and fan-out existed with 1.4.0.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A definition refresh waits for the serialized watcher update; native update broadcasts are on the policy-refresh path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace or notify an OS registry/managed-preferences watcher for a changed definition set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one replacement per effective changed set per centralized service; Throttler prevents concurrent creation within each service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior package version was invoked with the same whole-set API at exactly the same frequency. No changed code establishes extra polling, callbacks, allocations, or retained watcher state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watcher replacement must complete its initial callback before the queued update resolves.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of definition-change events, effective changed definition sets, policy keys in each update, and open renderer clients. Work is per event/set rather than one native boundary call per policy key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Definition replacement is serialized per service by Throttler. Equal managed-settings sets avoid replacement. Native callbacks are handled synchronously and then broadcast by the existing IPC event infrastructure; the diff adds no new parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current definition set and initialization promise suppress unchanged recreation and duplicate initialization. Native values are retained only for watched keys and pruned when definitions are removed. No cache key, invalidation, negative-cache, or retention policy changes in the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that repository-level event cardinality, serialization, cleanup ownership through MutableDisposable, and boundary placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native 1.6.0 implementation details are unavailable in the reviewed repository, so package-internal callback frequency or resource changes cannot be measured or inferred safely.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. A version bump alone does not prove that the native implementation performs more work or retains more resources.

Scenarios.Scenario: CLI process startup with native enterprise policies on Windows or macOS
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ConfigurationService.initialize updates policy definitions, dynamically imports policy-watcher, creates one watcher, and waits for its initial callback before CLI startup proceeds beyond configuration initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the native addon and perform the initial native policy read/watch subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One watcher initialization per CLI process and definition set on Windows/macOS.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initialization path and count used policy-watcher 1.4.0. The diff contains no evidence that 1.6.0 increases native work or delays the callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It is on ConfigurationService.initialize's startup critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One process-local product policy definition set; policy count affects one whole-set watcher creation rather than boundary calls per key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A per-service Throttler serializes updates. Startup performs a single cold initialization in the normal path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The module loader caches the imported addon in-process and the watcher remains live for the CLI process lifetime. There is no cross-process cache; each CLI process has one cold native watcher when enterprise policies are enabled.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the single-watcher critical path and unchanged invocation; low evidence for any cost delta inside the package.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The package artifact's internal startup cost is not represented in the diff and no benchmark or source change demonstrates a regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dependency installation or restoration for development and product builds
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold package-manager cache, npm fetches the selected policy-watcher tarball and runs its existing install script; this is part of dependency restoration. With a warm cache, the artifact can be reused according to npm cache behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the policy-watcher npm tarball when absent from the local cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One changed artifact fetch per cold dependency restore, subject to npm caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold restores fetched the 1.4.0 tarball instead; there was still one package fetch. No size or latency evidence establishes that the new artifact is more expensive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the dependency-install critical path, but only the artifact identity changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the package's native-addon install script.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One install-script execution for the package under the same installer conditions as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Version 1.4.0 also had hasInstallScript enabled; the diff does not add another script invocation or changed transitive build dependency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On native dependency restoration's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One policy-watcher package artifact per install target; the lockfile shows the same direct dependency shape and no newly added transitive packages.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Controlled by npm's existing installer scheduling. The diff does not add package-level fan-out, extra scripts, or a new dependency subtree.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold cache fetches the 1.6.0 tarball identified by the new URL/integrity; warm cache can reuse that exact artifact. Both old and new lock entries have an install script, and unchanged lockfile sections indicate no additional transitive dependency resolution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the network artifact identity changed while fetch and script cardinality did not; no evidence supports a cost increase.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tarball and install-script duration/size are not available in the supplied repository data.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. A different cached artifact URL without increased call count, dependency fan-out, or measured size/work is not a concrete performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file dependency-only diff. Traced desktop startup, policy refresh, CLI startup, and dependency installation, including native OS, IPC, network, and install-script boundaries. Repository-level scheduling, coalescing, watcher lifecycle, cardinality, and critical-path placement are unchanged, and the diff provides no concrete evidence of a regressive mechanism inside policy-watcher 1.6.0.
